sections.heading: Provenance, Legislative Objective & Doctrinal Foundations
sections.body: This topic covers s. 26–30 under the Indian Contract Act, 1872. Read the statutory scheme as a coherent allocation of rights, duties, conditions, defences and consequences.

sections.heading: Textual Anatomy, Provisos & Statutory Deconstruction
sections.body: s. 26–30 must be broken into definitions, operative words, conditions, exceptions, savings and consequences. Map the agreement and commercial records to each statutory ingredient.

sections.heading: Mandatory Proving Ingredients & Essential Elements
sections.body:
1. Establish the transaction and parties.
2. Identify the statutory trigger in s. 26–30.
3. Prove each constituent fact.
4. Test exceptions and defences.
5. Identify the precise legal consequence.

sections.heading: Evidentiary Burdens under BSA 2023 (ss. 104–106 & s. 63)
sections.body: The asserting party ordinarily bears the initial burden on essential facts, subject to admissions and statutory presumptions. Electronic records should be authenticated and presented under the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023.

sections.heading: Procedural Roadmap, Competent Forum & Limitation Act Checkpoints
sections.body: Check jurisdiction, limitation, arbitration or jurisdiction clauses, court fees and the exact relief. Verify the applicable Limitation Act Article and accrual date.

enhancement.detailedExplanation:
India Code rule: Sections 26–30 declare specified agreements void, including agreements in restraint of marriage, restraint of trade subject to the statutory exception, restraint of legal proceedings subject to statutory exceptions, uncertainty, and wagering agreements.

Definition: Void-agreement provisions identify classes of bargains that the Act refuses to enforce even though the parties may have reached apparent agreement.

Ingredients:
1. Identify the bargain and the specific restraint or uncertainty.
2. Match the facts to the exact statutory prohibition.
3. Check the statutory exceptions, especially those built into section 27 and section 28.
4. For wagers, identify the essential wagering characteristics rather than merely an uncertain commercial bargain.
examples: A agrees to pay B if a future uncertain event occurs and B has no interest in the event other than winning or losing the stake; the arrangement falls within the statutory treatment of wagering agreements.
problemApplication: Apply sections 26–30 to a factual problem by identifying the statutory trigger, testing every ingredient, checking exceptions or limitations, and stating the legal consequence.
keyTakeaways: Sections 26–30 declare specified agreements void, including agreements in restraint of marriage, restraint of trade subject to the statutory exception, restraint of legal proceedings subject to statutory exceptions, uncertainty, and wagering agreements.
Void-agreement provisions identify classes of bargains that the Act refuses to enforce even though the parties may have reached apparent agreement.
